sections.text: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः।
He who will study this spiritual discourse of ours, I assure thee, he shall thereby worship Me at the altar of Wisdom.
Yea, he who listens to it with faith and without doubt, even he, freed from evil, shall rise to the worlds which the virtuous attain through righteous deeds.
O Arjuna! Hast thou listened attentively to My words? Has thy ignorance and thy delusion gone?

So we had been discussing chapter 18, Moksha Sannyasa Yoga, Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation. This is the last chapter in Bhagavad Gita, and Bhagavan has given his final advice to us. It boils down to Sreyan Swadharma Vigunaha Paradharma Swanashti da.
Your own Dharma is better for you than other dharma. And therefore he says, Sahajam Karma Kamateja Sadosham Abhiyana Tej. These are the two basic facts.
He pointed out to us that your welfare is in staying within your Dharma, whatever Dharma you have acquired through your own choice. My dharma as an architect -- I chose it myself. I decided to go to architecture school and therefore I became an architect.
Bhagavan said, your welfare is in your Dharma. Dont try to practice something other than what youre good at. Then there was Sahajam Karma Kaunteya.
Do what comes naturally to you. Because of all your experiences and vasanas and tendencies and your training, there are few things in life which comes easier for you. And others dont stay with what comes naturally to you, even though other things look more glamorous, more glorious.
But you say, even if your Dharma, you found it Sadosha Mapi, even there are some defects in it or not very perfect. Do actions in your own field which come naturally to you. There are the only two things he said, doing so you will overcome all your obstacles and you will never incur sin.
Working in the field which come naturally to you, keeping your own goal in mind that Im doing it to get my ultimate happiness. But once you will never incur sin. Sin, as we have discussed, is a negative impression on my mind which creates agitations.
All we are looking for in life is peace. Give me peace of mind. Peace of mind only comes when the mind is tranquil.
Because the mind will only be tranquil if youre working according to your own Dharma. And then he said the final advice after completing his entire discourse: now you do whatever you think is right for you. He gave you the complete choice one more time and said, let me summarize what I told you.
Manmana Bhava mad Bhaktaha Madhya ji Mam namaskuruhu. In other words, Krishna said, if you want to summarize the entire teachings of Bhagavad Gita in half a verse, this is it. To get the happiness which you are looking for, fix your mind onto me -- me, the all-pervading almighty self which is also your self.
Focus your mind on that mad Bhaktah worship that identify with that Madhya Ji. Offer all your actions to me. Offer all your actions to the highest goal which you have when you go to the first grade.
Im learning this and that. Because eventually I want to become a doctor. My granddaughter was telling me yesterday, I have two inventions I want to release before I became a doctor.
So there is an ultimate goal in mind. That ultimate goal is to find perfect happiness. Perfect happiness is only there if my mind is tranquil.
Bhagawan said, Madhya Ji, offer everything to me Maam namaskurohu and take refuge in me. Then he clarified say Sarva Dharma and parity. Aham TVA Sarva Papebiha Moksa Kshya minasucha.
Right now you think that you are incomplete. You have lots of baggage -- all your incompleteness and sins, the things which you have not done right. I have not done this thing right in my life. Bhagawan said, no, you cannot correct yourself on your own. But if you take refuge in me, I can correct that.
Sarva Dharman Parityajya. And we have discussed this Sarva Dharman. Every role that I take, it comes with its own Dharma.
Every role a drama actor plays, it comes with its own requirement. Now if I start identifying with each role, then Ill get confused. I will have a nervous breakdown.
I will have a personality disorder. I dont know who I am. Am I a king or a pauper? Because I play so many different roles.
The Bhagawan says, in your life, you take on too many of these roles. All those roles come with their own Dharma. My Dharma as a father.
My Dharma as an architect. My Dharma as a husband. My Dharma as a citizen of this country.
My Dharma as an employer. All those Dharmas -- if I get bogged down into them and think that they will give me my happiness, then Ill be completely shattered. I do not really know which role is more important than others.
Keep working in that dharma when you are there. When you are an architect, act as an architect. When you are father, act as a father.
But at the end of the day, you realize that you are something other than all the roles which you play. An actor in Beverly Hills knows that he is something other than the roles he plays. So Bhagawanja Sarva Dharma and Paritya Jya.
At the end of the day, give up. All those dharmas are not yours. But they belong to the roles which you play.
While youre playing that role, you cant give up those dharmas. But once youre out of that role, leave those dharmas with that role and focus on who you are. Who is there One constant in all these roles which has its own dharma.
So Bhagawan says, ma makeam sharam Braja. Identify with that one single entity which is pervading through all the roles which you play. Ahamtva Sarva Pape bihamoksik Shami Mashu chah.
Once you identify with that, all the limitations you have in each one of those roles are of no consequence because it only belongs to the role. You may not have played the role correctly. Fine, lets move on to the next one.
One movie gets flopped, the actor doesnt get shattered. He moves on to another one, waiting for the next hit. Dont get caught up in any of those roles as thats the only thing which is mine.
And if I fail there, I have failed in it. Bhagavan said, you dont worry. Once you take refuge in your own self, everything will be alright.
Now that you have learnt this knowledge, dont just sit back and relax. Thats not where your duty ends. You have to do your part.
Now that you were privileged enough to know what is right, you also have an obligation to teach others what is right. And I, the parent, was a son at one point of time. And I got the advice from my parents and they told me what is right and wrong.
I made my life right or wrong according to that. And now I learned after my experience what is right and wrong. I have an obligation to pass on that knowledge to my children.
Ya Imam paramam guhiyam mad bhakteshu abhi dashyathi bhakti mai param kutva Mama eva isyati asansaya. He said, there is one who declares this, teaches this knowledge of mine to my devotees, not to the people who are not interested in it, but those who are inspired themselves to make their life better, make their life appropriate, remove all the negatives from their life, but they still do not know how to do it. When you find those enthusiastic students, thats what you want to teach them.
Therefore I said, the one who teaches this sacred knowledge of mind to my Bhakta, those who are devoted to this knowledge, Bhakti mai param kutva maam eva Eshyati asansayaha. I consider that he is worshipping me. Bhagavan said, you dont have to come to my temple every day and put $1 in the Aarti or to do anything special.
The greatest devotion we can offer to our teacher is to carry the torch of his knowledge. Thats why we do Pada Puja. Because the platform on which my Guru is standing that the platform which I worship, that knowledge is important.
Bhagawan said, one who spread this knowledge of mine which I gave it to you, to others, I consider him to be my devotee and therefore he will come to me without any doubt. He will become one with me or Sansayah. No other thing needed.
Bhagavan said, you just continue. You learn this knowledge, practice it, and then pass it on to the others. That Bhagavan said, I consider to my greatest devotion.
So basically it encourages all of us, whatever little we have learned from Bhagavad Gita. There is an obligation to impart the knowledge to someone else who is curious to know. He may not have the right frame of understanding, but he wants to know.
You have an obligation to give him that knowledge. Bhagawan says, Nachatasmat manushesu kaschinmi priyakrutamaha. None other than that person who carries this torch of knowledge is dearer to me than him.
He is the closest to me because hes carrying forward the mission that I have -- that I want to correct the misunderstanding in people. You were confused, Arjuna. I gave you this discourse so that you can now act in your life correctly.
Now you have an obligation to do that to someone else who you will find it in the same situation. And I consider that as my worship that you have appreciated what I have given you. And such a person is dearer to me.
Some other people may come and other things for me, but they are of lesser value than you carrying forward my mission. Bhavita Nachame tasmat anyaha Priyatara Bhuvi, not only now, but even in future, there wont be anyone who is dearer to me than the one who is spreading this knowledge to make this world better and spreading the right knowledge. So we have this misconception in our Hinduism -- that we obviously dont convert people, we dont encourage people to come to our fold.
In fact, we discourage people: If someone has to be Hindu, you cant become a Hindu unless youre born Hindu. Sri Bhagawan clearly points out that thats not part of our culture. We do not want forced conversion. We dont want to tell people who have not yet understood to believe in this knowledge.
Give him his own time. Because forced conversion, forced imposition, never works in reality anywhere. Therefore you say, find people who are willing to understand this and give this knowledge.
Thats your obligation. So thats a kind of missionary work. They never said that this knowledge should never be given out to anybody, or that it should not be given to people who are not from this class or the other.
Simply: find the right person, the right group of people who are anxious to make their lives better. Give this knowledge to them. Ill consider that the greatest devotion to me.
And he said, such a person is dear to me not only now, but this will never change. Its not that right now Im telling you this, but in the future it may be something different. It will hold true throughout history: whoever spreads his teachers knowledge is the greatest devotee, and that is the greatest Guru Dakshina one can give to his teacher.
Now, lets say you consider that you are not capable of spreading this knowledge -- you dont have the resources, you dont have the temperament, you dont consider yourself worthy of doing so. But if you just listen to this: Adhyeshyate Cha Imam Dharmyam Samvadam Avayoho. This dialogue of ours, this sacred dialogue which deals with who you are in reality and who you are not, how to act in this world so that you can achieve your ultimate goal.
This dialogue which we had, which is sacred, even if you just study that listening is slightly different than studying one who studies this.

These verses address studying and listening to the Gita. Verse 70: one who studies this dharmya-samvada (sacred dialogue) worships through jnana-yajna (knowledge-sacrifice). Verse 71: even one who merely listens with shraddha (faith) and without anasuya (fault-finding) becomes liberated and reaches the auspicious worlds of the righteous. Verse 72 is Krishnas final question to Arjuna: Have you listened with one-pointed mind? Has your delusion born of ignorance been destroyed?
The distinction between studying and listening is significant. Studying is active engagement - reading, contemplating, discussing. Listening is receptive - allowing the teaching to enter without immediate analysis or judgment. Both are valid paths. The key qualifier for listening is shraddha (faith) and absence of anasuya (carping criticism). Coming to spiritual teachings looking for flaws prevents any transmission. Coming with openness allows transformation.
How do you engage with spiritual teachings? Are you a student - actively working with the material, questioning, applying? Or a listener - receptively allowing wisdom to seep in? Both have value. Today, try the approach less natural to you. If you typically analyze, simply listen without judgment. If you typically receive passively, actively wrestle with one teaching. And honestly ask yourself Krishnas question: Has your ignorance-born delusion been dispelled? If confusion remains, that is honest and workable. But if there is pretense of understanding without genuine transformation, that is the real obstacle.
